transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Since the V-12 vision-inspection station commissioning is scheduled for this weekend, I'd like to get our pre-work review started. Before I approve the work order, I need to check in with maintenance, quality, and safety. We also need to finalize whether the station goes at Cell 3 or Cell 7 — both produce the same product family, so I'd like to hear from each of you on any factors that should drive that placement decision. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should start with what I've found. During my fit-up check, the V-12 camera mount aligns only with Cell 7's 6 mm bracket pattern — it won't fit Cell 3. Installing at Cell 7 requires exactly 4 hours and isolation of exactly 3 electrical points. I recorded all these measurements in the weekend commissioning file, but it's still awaiting engineering signoff and hasn't been added to the work-order summary yet, so that's why it wasn't in front of everyone until now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something important for the commissioning plan. I reviewed the customer validation appendix this morning, and release requires exactly 30 signed reference samples followed by challenge testing on exactly 100 consecutive production pieces. The quality checklist has not yet been revised because the customer appendix is still being attached to the change record, so the current checklist doesn't reflect these requirements yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a safety requirement before the work order is approved. During my safety walkdown of the V-12, I found that the access-door interlock must be tested through exactly 6 open-and-trip cycles before commissioning, with the results recorded in an interlock test record. The permit draft is currently waiting for my walkdown notes and does not yet contain that test count, so it's not reflected in the paperwork everyone has seen.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Ensure the V-12 fit-up findings (Cell 7 bracket alignment, 4 hours, 3 electrical isolation points) are added to the work-order summary and receive engineering signoff before the work order is approved.

Ensure the customer validation appendix is attached to the change record and the quality checklist is revised to reflect 30 signed reference samples and 100 consecutive challenge test pieces before commissioning begins.
Ensure walkdown notes including the 6 open-and-trip interlock test cycles are incorporated into the permit draft before the work order is approved.
Work order will not be approved until maintenance, quality, and safety documentation gaps are resolved and all three check-ins are satisfactorily completed.
